Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Implement GitHub issue #37, "R1 03: Sign-in with AuthKit and Organization creation", in chrisdoc/surveybeat-next. This is production code and security-sensitive (sessions, account linking), so be careful and explicit. You're in your own git worktree. Check it's at origin/main (`git fetch origin && git log -1 origin/main`), which holds slices 01, 02, 05, and 14: the workspace, the packages, the oxlint plugin, an Alchemy v2 stack with `pr-<n>` preview stages, email sending (EmailSender, send states, React Email), and the privacy suite (`pnpm test:privacy`, the endpoint privacy registry in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`, preview-privacy and e2e jobs).

## First
- Run `gh issue view 37 --comments`. It has the acceptance criteria and two setup comments (secrets, WorkOS project and environment ids, redirect URIs). Follow them exactly.
- Create branch `t3/r1-03-sign-in` from origin/main.
- Read GLOSSARY.md, docs/adr/0002-people-join-by-being-added.md, docs/adr/0003-organization-admin-sees-no-results.md, docs/adr/0008, docs/research/workos-authkit-workers.md (the key reference: the `@workos-inc/node` workerd build, sealed sessions, refresh, revocation catch, self-serve org creation), docs/infra.md, infra/alchemy.run.ts, and packages/cloudflare/src/*.

## Key requirements (also in #37)
- AuthKit hosted UI: the six-digit email code, Google, Microsoft. The Main Worker handles `/auth/login`, `/auth/callback`, and `/auth/logout`, with a sealed session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax), refresh, and logout. Use `@workos-inc/node` (exact pin; respect pnpm minimumReleaseAge and never add minimumReleaseAgeExclude), constructed per isolate from `env`.
- **Per-request session check:** local JWT verification plus our own deny check (revoked session, Person removed, Membership ended). Access tokens last about 5 minutes. SPEC §6.2: don't use KV for sessions that must be revoked at once. Decide where the deny list lives (D1 or the Organization DO) and record why.
- **First sign-in with no matching Person:**
  - an email on the allowlist (`ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST` secret, comma-separated, read per stage) sees "Create an Organization" (name only). This is idempotent per WorkOS user (double submits and retries create exactly one), and the creator becomes the Organization admin, with WorkOS org role `admin`;
  - anyone else sees "You're not part of an Organization yet".
- **Linking:** a WorkOS user links to a Person only by an exact match on a VERIFIED email. An unverified email never links. A verified email that matches Persons in several Organizations gets an Organization picker.
- **D1 global index** (`packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/`): WorkOS user → Persons, and email → Organizations for Persons not yet linked. Design the schema. Tokens and emails are case-normalised. No survey content.
- Secrets reach Workers through Alchemy (`Config.Redacted`), and in CI through the GitHub secrets `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST`. Wire them into `.github/workflows/preview.yml`. Also generate a cookie-sealing password per stage (Alchemy `Random`, or a secret).
- **Verify the WorkOS key on the first preview deploy:** the redirect URIs are configured ONLY on the SurveyBeat Staging environment, so if the key belongs to another environment, sign-in fails. Add a smoke check that the authorization URL for the stage is accepted, or explain how you verified it.
- Configure WorkOS logout URIs for the same hosts with `workos authkit logout-uris set --environment-id REDACTED ...` (the CLI is logged in on this host). Also report whether Email code, Google, and Microsoft are enabled. If the CLI can't show this, say so and don't guess.
- The web app gets minimal screens: Sign in, Create an Organization, Not part of an Organization, and the Organization picker. Use the message catalog, Tailwind, and Base UI. TanStack Router may be added now if needed (exact pin).
- New endpoints are classified in `privacyRegistry` (none return Result data).

## Tests
- API tests for every first-sign-in branch (allowlisted, not allowlisted, existing Person by verified email, unverified email never links, several Organizations → picker), idempotent creation, and revocation taking effect on the next request.
- WorkOS is faked behind a domain interface in unit tests. No `any`, and no `as` outside tests.
- Extend the Playwright e2e at least to "the login redirect reaches the AuthKit domain".

## Validation
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `typecheck`, `typecheck:effect`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, `test:privacy` all pass.

## Shipping
- Commit on `t3/r1-03-sign-in` with a succinct message ending with:
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- Push, and open a PR to main titled "R1 03: Sign-in with AuthKit and Organization creation". The body says "Closes #37. Part of #34.", lists the changes and the decisions (the deny-list location, the D1 schema, the cookie settings), and ends with:
  `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`
- Do not merge. Last line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

- Check whether WorkOS accepts wildcard redirect URIs for `pr-<n>` stages. If it doesn't, document the workaround.

API tests for every branch of first sign-in. A test that an unverified email doesn't link. A test that revocation takes effect on the next request.

# WorkOS AuthKit from a Cloudflare Worker (no Next.js SDK)

Research for issue #7 (map #1). Context: SPEC.md §5.6 (sign-in, Directory Sync, roles) and §6.1 (the Worker handles the OAuth callback, keeps a session cookie, checks it on every request, and verifies WorkOS webhooks).

Researched 2026-11-07 against `@workos-inc/node` v12.2.0 (released 2026-11-05) and the WorkOS docs.

## TL;DR

- **Use `@workos-inc/node` directly in the Worker.** Its `package.json` has a `workerd` export condition that resolves to `lib/index.worker.mjs`. That build uses `fetch` and Web Crypto (`SubtleCryptoProvider`), and it bundles `iron-webcrypto` and `jose` inline. Wrangler or esbuild picks the `workerd` condition on its own. You can also import `@workos-inc/node/worker` explicitly. Source: [package.json](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/package.json), [src/index.worker.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/index.worker.ts).
- **Everything the spec needs exists in that SDK**: the hosted-UI authorization URL, the code exchange with a sealed cookie, `loadSealedSession().authenticate()` (local JWKS check), `refresh()`, the logout URL, `revokeSession`, organizations, memberships, invitations, and `webhooks.constructEvent`.
- **Catch 1: "magic link" is a code.** AuthKit Magic Auth emails a six-digit one-time code, not a clickable link.
- **Catch 2: revocation is not immediate under local JWT checks.** An access token stays valid until its `exp`, even after its session is revoked. To meet SPEC's "lose access immediately", the Worker needs its own deny check on each request (see §5).
- **Catch 3: self-serve Organizations are app code.** AuthKit does not create an Organization at sign-up. The app does it: create the Organization, create the membership, then refresh with `organizationId`.
- **Optional helper:** `@workos/authkit-session` (v0.9.1, *prerelease*) is a framework-agnostic toolkit that uses `Request`/`Response`, `iron-webcrypto`, `jose`, and `valibot`, and has no Node APIs. It's useful as a reference. Pinning a prerelease is optional. Source: [workos/authkit-session README](https://github.com/workos/authkit-session).

## 1. Packages and the Workers runtime

| Package | Runs in Workers? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@workos-inc/node` ≥ v7.x (current 12.2.0) | **Yes** | Its `exports` map has `workerd`, `edge-light`, and `convex` conditions that point to `lib/index.worker.{mjs,cjs}`, plus an explicit `./worker` subpath. `WorkOSWorker` overrides `createHttpClient` with `FetchHttpClient` and `getCryptoProvider` with `SubtleCryptoProvider`. `inlinedDependencies` contains `iron-webcrypto` 2.0.0, `jose` 6.2.12, and `uint8array-extras`. The repo's `scripts/ecosystem-check.ts` imports the SDK under **miniflare**, and it checks that "the worker entry bundles cleanly without node builtins". [package.json](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/package.json), [index.worker.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/index.worker.ts), [ecosystem-check.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/scripts/ecosystem-check.ts) |
| `@workos/authkit-session` 0.9.1 | Yes (by design) | Prerelease ("APIs may change without notice"). Includes `AuthKitCore` (JWKS with caching, session encryption, refresh orchestration), `AuthOperations`, and `CookieSessionStorage<Request, Response>`. [repo](https://github.com/workos/authkit-session) |
| `@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs`, `authkit-remix`, `authkit-react-router`, `authkit-tanstack-start`, `authkit-astro`, `authkit-sveltekit` | Not applicable | Framework glue. SPEC rules out Next.js. |
| `@workos-inc/authkit-js` / `authkit-react` | Browser | Client-side PKCE SDKs that keep the refresh token in the browser. They don't fit, because §6.1 wants the Worker to hold the session. |

WorkOS announced Workers support in 2024. That release replaced Node `http` and `crypto` with Fetch and Web Crypto ([blog](https://workos.com/blog/launch-week-spring-2024-day-4-cloudflare-workers-edge-support)).

**Official Cloudflare examples:** no first-party AuthKit plus plain-Worker sample exists. The closest are:
- [workos/mcp-shop-cloudflare](https://github.com/workos/mcp-shop-cloudflare): an MCP server on Workers with AuthKit OAuth. Relevant to SPEC §5.7's MCP server.
- The 2024 blog's webhook Worker that uses `itty-router` (see §8 for a caveat about its body handling).
- An open PR adding Cloudflare deploy to the [authkit-tanstack-start example](https://github.com/workos/authkit-tanstack-start).

Construct the client once per isolate, inside `fetch`, because secrets live on `env`: `new WorkOS(env.WORKOS_API_KEY, { clientId: env.WORKOS_CLIENT_ID })`. The SDK caches the JWKS on the `UserManagement` instance (`createRemoteJWKSet` with a five-minute cooldown). If you memoize the client per isolate, the JWKS cache survives between requests ([user-management.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/user-management.ts)).

## 2. Hosted UI and OAuth callback flow

1. **`GET /login`** redirects to `workos.userManagement.getAuthorizationUrl({ provider: 'authkit', clientId, redirectUri, state, screenHint?, loginHint?, organizationId? })`.
   - `provider`, `connectionId`, and `organizationId` are mutually exclusive connection selectors, and exactly one is required.
   - `screenHint` takes `'sign-in'` or `'sign-up'` and works only with `authkit`.
   - `state` comes back unchanged on the redirect. Use it for CSRF protection plus a return-to path.
   - `getAuthorizationUrlWithPKCE` also exists, but PKCE is optional for a confidential server client.
   - Sources: [Get authorization URL](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/authentication/get-authorization-url), [user-management.ts `getAuthorizationUrl`](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/user-management.ts).
2. **`GET /callback?code&state`**: check `state` against a short-lived cookie. Then call `workos.userManagement.authenticateWithCode({ clientId, code, session: { sealSession: true, cookiePassword } })`. The call returns `user`, `organizationId`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, and `sealedSession`. The code is valid for 10 minutes ([Node AuthKit guide](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/vanilla/nodejs)).
3. Set `wos-session=<sealedSession>` with `Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` (same guide).
4. In the dashboard, configure the Redirect URI, the Initiate login URI, and the Sign-out URI. Logout errors out if no Sign-out URI is set (same guide).

## 3. Session cookie sealing and per-request validation

- **Sealing:** `sealData`/`unsealData` wrap **iron-webcrypto** with a versioned seal (`~2`) and a password of at least 32 characters (`WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD`). The seal contains the access token, the refresh token, the user, and the impersonator. Sources: [seal.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/common/crypto/seal.ts), [session.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/session.ts).
- **Per request:** `const s = workos.userManagement.loadSealedSession({ sessionData, cookiePassword }); const r = await s.authenticate();` This unseals the cookie, then calls `verifyAccessToken`. That runs `jose.jwtVerify` against the remote JWKS and checks the issuer when one is configured. It then checks the claims a user token needs: `sub`, `sid`, `iss`, `exp`, `iat`, and `auth_time`. Agent and widget tokens are rejected. No network call is made once the JWKS is cached.
  - On success, it returns `{ authenticated: true, sessionId, organizationId, role, roles, permissions, entitlements, featureFlags, user, accessToken }`.
  - On failure, `reason` is one of `no_session_cookie_provided`, `invalid_session_cookie`, or `invalid_jwt`.
  - JWKS or network errors throw. They are not treated as an invalid session.
  - Source: [session.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/session.ts), [user-management.ts `verifyAccessToken`](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/user-management.ts).
- **JWKS:** `https://api.workos.com/sso/jwks/{client_id}`, also available from `getJwksUrl(clientId)`. Access token claims include `sid`, `org_id`, `role`, `roles`, `permissions`, `entitlements`, `feature_flags`, `exp`, and others. The docs' example token lives for 300 s ([Session tokens](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/session-tokens)). The lifetime is configurable in Dashboard → Sessions, and WorkOS recommends keeping it short ([Sessions](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/sessions)).
- **Effect fit:** wrap `authenticate()` in an `Effect.tryPromise` service. Map the `reason` values to typed errors, and treat thrown errors as `Unavailable`, not `Unauthenticated`.

## 4. Refresh

- When `authenticate()` fails with `invalid_jwt` (the token expired), call `await s.refresh({ organizationId? })`. It calls `authenticateWithRefreshToken` and reseals the cookie. It returns `{ authenticated, sealedSession, ...claims }`. The caller must write the new `Set-Cookie`. If it doesn't, every request refreshes again ([session.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/session.ts), [authkit-session README](https://github.com/workos/authkit-session)).
- Refresh tokens are **single-use and rotate** ([Session tokens](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/session-tokens)). A **30-second replay grace period** makes concurrent or retried refreshes "converge on one result". That matters for an SPA that sends parallel API calls with the same expired cookie.
  - After the 30 seconds, an old token returns `invalid_grant`.
  - Treat timeouts, 5xx, and 429 as transient: keep the session and retry.
  - Sign the user out **only** on a terminal `invalid_grant`.
  - The SDK sorts these cases into terminal (`retryable: false`) and retryable results.
  - Source: [Session resilience](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/session-resilience).
- `refresh({ organizationId })` is also how a user **switches Organization** and how the app gets an `org_id` after creating one (§7).
- Session limits: the maximum session length and the inactivity timeout (no refresh within the window) are set in the dashboard. The required ordering is access token duration < inactivity timeout < max session length ([Sessions](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/sessions), [WorkOS blog](https://workos.com/blog/session-length-access-token-duration-inactivity-timeout)).

## 5. Sign-out and immediate revocation

- **Sign-out:** handle `POST /logout`, which needs CSRF protection. Call `await s.getLogoutUrl({ returnTo? })`, which builds `https://api.workos.com/user_management/sessions/logout?session_id=<sid>&return_to=…`. Clear the cookie, then redirect. WorkOS ends its session and sends the user to the Sign-out URI ([Node guide](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/vanilla/nodejs), [user-management.ts `getLogoutUrl`](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/user-management/user-management.ts)).
- **Revoke from the server:** `workos.userManagement.revokeSession({ sessionId })` calls `POST /user_management/sessions/revoke`. `listSessions(userId)` lists a user's sessions ([Session API](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/session)).
- **Deactivating an organization membership revokes all of that user's active sessions** ([Users and organizations](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/users-organizations.md)).
- **But revocation is not instant for local verification:** revoking "stops the session from being refreshed, but tokens already issued remain valid until they expire" ([WorkOS blog](https://workos.com/blog/session-length-access-token-duration-inactivity-timeout); also [stateless JWT logout](https://workos.com/blog/stateless-jwt-logout-problem)).
- **Recommendation for SPEC §5.6 ("lose access immediately"):**
  - Keep the access token short, for example 5 minutes.
  - On each request, also look up SurveyBeat's own Person or Membership state in D1 or KV, which is needed for authorization anyway.
  - Keep a revoked-`sid` deny set, fed by `session.revoked`, `organization_membership.updated`/`deleted`, `dsync.user.deleted`, and `user.deleted` events.
  - This makes revocation immediate. The JWT check only proves who the caller is.

## 6. Magic link, Google, Microsoft

All three are enabled in the Dashboard → Authentication. AuthKit's hosted page then shows them, with no code changes ([Social login](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/social-login)).

- **Magic Auth:** an emailed **six-digit, one-time code that expires after 10 minutes**, not a link ([Magic Auth](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/magic-auth)). SPEC §5.6 says "email magic link", so the product owner should accept a code. If a clickable link is required, build a custom UI with `createMagicAuth` and `authenticateWithMagicAuth` (both in the SDK).
- **Google:** in staging, WorkOS's default credentials work. In **production you must supply your own Google client ID and secret**, and register the WorkOS redirect URI from Dashboard → Authentication → OAuth providers → Google. Direct provider value: `GoogleOAuth` ([Google OAuth](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/google-oauth)).
- **Microsoft:** same pattern, with your own Azure app registration in production, a Web-platform redirect URI, and provider value `MicrosoftOAuth` ([Microsoft OAuth](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/microsoft-oauth)).
  - **Watch out:** the page currently says to pick "Personal Microsoft accounts only" under Supported Account Types, which looks wrong for B2B work accounts. Confirm this with WorkOS or test it before production.
- **Enterprise SSO (SAML/OIDC):** pass `organizationId` (or `connectionId`) to `getAuthorizationUrl`, or let AuthKit route by domain.

## 7. Self-serve: create a WorkOS Organization at first sign-in

AuthKit does not do this on its own. The documented pattern ([Users and organizations](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/users-organizations.md)):

1. After the callback, check whether the result or the token has an `org_id`.
2. If it has none, show a "name your organization" form. Then call `workos.organizations.createOrganization({ name, externalId? })` and `workos.userManagement.createOrganizationMembership({ userId, organizationId, roleSlug: 'admin' })`.
3. Call `session.refresh({ organizationId })` (or `authenticateWithRefreshToken({ organizationId })`) to get a token scoped to that organization, then reseal the cookie.

Make this idempotent, because users double-submit and Workers retry. Store the SurveyBeat Organization row keyed by the WorkOS org id. Setting `externalId` to SurveyBeat's id helps here. Users can also be JIT-provisioned into an existing Organization when their email matches one of its verified domains (same page).

## 8. Inviting People who have not signed in

- `workos.userManagement.sendInvitation({ email, organizationId, roleSlug?, expiresInDays? (1–30, default 7), inviterUserId?, locale? })`. Invitation states are `pending`, `accepted`, `expired`, and `revoked`. The invitation object includes `token` and `accept_invitation_url`. Other calls: `resendInvitation`, `revokeInvitation`, `findInvitationByToken`, `listInvitations` ([Invitation API](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/invitation)).
- "Invitations are for both new users and existing users." A new user gets a sign-up link and "automatically join[s] the organization". The membership stays `pending` until they accept ([Invitations](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/invitations), [Users and organizations](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/users-organizations.md)).
- **Email sending:** WorkOS sends the invitation email by default. Sending it yourself is supported. SPEC §5.8 wants Cloudflare Email Service for invitations, so use the `accept_invitation_url` in our own template. Before accepting, check that the invitee's email matches, using `findInvitationByToken`. The exact setting that turns off WorkOS's email isn't clearly documented, so check the dashboard's email settings. Sandbox limit: 100 invitation emails per 24 hours.
- Domain mapping: create the SurveyBeat Person when we invite, with an email and no WorkOS user id. Link the Person on the `invitation.accepted` and `organization_membership.created` events, or at the first callback.

## 9. Organization roles

- Roles have immutable slugs. The environment default role is `member` and can't be deleted. Define an `admin` role yourself in the dashboard; it isn't built in. Organization-specific custom roles (prefixed `org`) are also possible. Each membership has one role by default, and multiple roles can be turned on ([Roles and permissions](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/roles-and-permissions)).
- Roles are set through the membership APIs (`roleSlug` on create, update, and invite), SSO or directory group mapping, or the dashboard. A change emits `organization_membership.updated`.
- The access token carries `role`, `roles`, and `permissions` for the current organization ([Session tokens](https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/session-tokens)). A role change reaches the token only at the next refresh, which is a reason to keep token lifetimes short. Team roles (lead, member, viewer) stay in SurveyBeat's data, as SPEC §5.6 says.

## 10. Verifying webhooks in a Worker, and the Events API

- **Header:** `WorkOS-Signature: t=<ms epoch>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`. The signature is computed over `` `${t}.${rawBody}` `` with the endpoint secret.
- **SDK:** `await workos.webhooks.constructEvent({ payload, sigHeader, secret, tolerance = 180000 })`. This runs on `SubtleCryptoProvider` with a constant-time compare, checks the timestamp tolerance (3 minutes), and **parses only after verification succeeds**.
- **Pass the raw body:** use `await request.text()`, not `request.json()`. The SDK accepts objects, but it would re-serialize them, and that may not match the exact bytes that were signed. The 2024 blog example passes parsed JSON, so don't copy it.
- Sources: [Webhooks](https://workos.com/docs/events/data-syncing/webhooks), [signature-provider.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/common/crypto/signature-provider.ts), [webhooks.ts](https://github.com/workos/workos-node/blob/main/src/webhooks/webhooks.ts).
- **Delivery:**
  - Any non-2xx response counts as a failure. Production retries up to 6 times with exponential backoff over 3 days. Staging retries only for a few minutes.
  - Delivery is **not ordered**, and duplicates are possible. Upsert using `updated_at` and dedupe on the event id.
  - WorkOS publishes a list of 15 source IPs that you can allowlist.
  - Pattern: verify, enqueue to a Cloudflare Queue, and return 200 quickly.
  - Source: [Webhooks](https://workos.com/docs/events/data-syncing/webhooks).
- **Events API:** `workos.events.listEvents({ events: [...], after?, rangeStart? })` lets you poll with a cursor. It keeps events for **90 days** and returns at most 30 days per request. WorkOS recommends processing events in order and storing the cursor after each one. Event ids are the same as in webhooks ([Events API](https://workos.com/docs/events/data-syncing/events-api)). A Cron Trigger plus a cursor in D1 makes a good **reconciliation backstop** for missed webhooks. Both paths can feed one idempotent handler.
- **Relevant events** ([Events](https://workos.com/docs/events)):
  - `user.created`, `user.updated`, `user.deleted`
  - `session.created`, `session.revoked`
  - `organization.*`
  - `organization_membership.created`, `organization_membership.updated`, `organization_membership.deleted`
  - `invitation.created`, `invitation.accepted`, `invitation.revoked`, `invitation.resent`
  - `dsync.user.*`, `dsync.group.*`, `dsync.group.user_added`, `dsync.group.user_removed`
  - `role.*`, `organization_role.*`

## Open points for the product owner or architecture

1. Is a six-digit email code acceptable as SPEC's "magic link"? If not, we need a custom UI for that one method.
2. Microsoft's "Personal accounts only" instruction in the WorkOS docs needs testing before production.
3. Decide on the deny check (revoked `sid` plus Person status in D1/KV) as the mechanism for "immediate" revocation, and set the access token lifetime (5 min suggested).
4. Use `@workos-inc/node` directly (stable). Possibly borrow from `@workos/authkit-session` (prerelease), but don't depend on it yet.

# SurveyBeat

SurveyBeat measures how a team is doing over time through short recurring check-ins, and helps the team act on what it learns.

## Tenancy and people

**Organization**:
The tenant. Every other record belongs to exactly one Organization, and data never crosses Organizations.
_Avoid_: Tenant, company, account, workspace

**Person**:
A human in an Organization, who may exist before ever signing in (imported or invited).
_Avoid_: User, employee, respondent

**Organization admin**:
A Person who administers an Organization: its Teams, Leads, and People. Being an admin gives no access to any Team's Results.
_Avoid_: Owner, superuser, account admin

**Team**:
A named group of People, optionally nested inside another Team.
_Avoid_: Group, squad, department (a department is just a parent Team)

**Membership**:
A Person's role (lead, member, or viewer) in one Team over a date range.
_Avoid_: Seat, assignment

**Lead**:
A Person holding the lead role in a Team's Membership.
_Avoid_: Manager, owner, admin

## Asking

**Question**:
A reusable item in the Organization's question library, with a type and text.
_Avoid_: Item, field, prompt

**Question version**:
One meaning of a Question. Answers always point at a Question version, never at the Question itself.
_Avoid_: Revision, edit

**Dimension**:
A theme a Question measures, such as workload or psychological safety, used to group scores.
_Avoid_: Category, topic, factor

**Template**:
A ready-made starting set of Questions, grouped by Dimension, that a Lead copies to create a Pulse. The Pulse does not change when its Template changes.
_Avoid_: Preset, blueprint

**Pulse**:
A recurring check-in for one Team: an ordered set of Question versions, a cadence, an answer window, an anonymity mode, and a distribution (invitation or link).
_Avoid_: Survey, questionnaire, form

**One-off survey**:
A Pulse with no cadence and exactly one Round. Not a separate concept.
_Avoid_: Survey (when meaning the concept)

**Distribution**:
How a Pulse reaches people: by Invitation (one per eligible member, so response rates are known) or by shared link (no Invitations, no response rate, no one-answer-per-person guarantee). Fixed per Pulse.
_Avoid_: Channel (that means email, Slack, or Teams)

**Channel**:
The medium an Invitation travels through: email, Slack, or Microsoft Teams.
_Avoid_: Distribution, transport

**Round**:
One occurrence of a Pulse, with its Question versions and eligible members frozen when it opens.
_Avoid_: Instance, iteration, run, wave

**Anonymity mode**:
A Pulse's privacy setting: anonymous, attributed, or confidential.
_Avoid_: Privacy level

**Minimum group size**:
The smallest number of contributors (N) any shown aggregate, comment, theme, or breakdown must have.
_Avoid_: Threshold (ambiguous), k

## Answering

**Invitation**:
One eligible member's single-use ticket to answer one Round, carrying an unguessable token.
_Avoid_: Link, ticket, request

**Participation record**:
The fact that a member answered a Round, held apart from what they answered.
_Avoid_: Completion, response (ambiguous)

**Submission**:
The set of Answers given in one Round by one respondent. In anonymous Rounds it carries no Person and no time.
_Avoid_: Response, entry, reply

**Answer**:
One value for one Question version within a Submission.
_Avoid_: Response, value

**Edit key**:
A random secret held only by a member's browser that lets them change their anonymous Submission.
_Avoid_: Token (that is the Invitation's)

**Contributor**:
A Submission counted toward one shown aggregate, because it gave that Question (or that Dimension's Questions) a value. The minimum group size counts Contributors per aggregate.
_Avoid_: Respondent, responder

## Understanding and acting

**Result**:
The derived, recomputable aggregate of a closed Round: scores, response rate, and Comment themes.
_Avoid_: Report, analytics, stats

**Typical change**:
How much a Team's score for one Question or Dimension usually moves from one Round to the next, judged from the Team's own history. A change well beyond it is shown as larger than usual.
_Avoid_: Significance, noise threshold, variance

**Redaction**:
Replacing names of the Organization's People, contact details, handles, and links in a comment with placeholders before anyone can read it.
_Avoid_: Anonymization, scrubbing, masking

**Comment theme**:
A machine-written summary of a group of comments, with a label, sentiment, count, and redacted quotes.
_Avoid_: Cluster, topic, insight

**Action**:
A commitment the Team makes in response to a Result, with an owner, a due date, and a status.
_Avoid_: Action item, task, todo

**Note**:
The Lead's free-text summary of a team discussion, visible to the Team.
_Avoid_: Comment (that is free text in an Answer)
# People join an Organization only by being added, and are linked by verified email

In Release 1, a sign-in never creates or joins an Organization on its own. Creating an Organization is self-serve but limited to an operator allowlist, because an open Organization lets anyone have SurveyBeat email arbitrary addresses from our domain, and Cloudflare Email Sending allows transactional mail only. Everyone else joins because a Lead or an Organization admin added them. Adding someone creates a Person (email only) and a Membership, and sends one "you've been added" email of our own. No WorkOS invitation is sent. When that Person first signs in, the Worker links their WorkOS user to the Person by an exact match on a verified email, and only then creates the WorkOS organization membership.

## Considered Options

- **WorkOS invitations.** Rejected: members answer Rounds without ever signing in, so a pending invitation that expires in 7–30 days is the wrong model, and it would send a second, WorkOS-branded email.
- **Joining automatically by verified email domain (WorkOS JIT).** Deferred to Release 3 with SSO. Free-mail domains make it unreliable for small teams.
- **Blocking a second Organization for the same company.** Rejected for Release 1: warning someone that "example.com already uses SurveyBeat" tells outsiders who our customers are.

## Consequences

The global index needs an email → Organizations lookup for Persons with no WorkOS user yet. A sign-in with an unverified email never links. Two Organizations for one company can exist and cannot be merged until a later release decides how.
# Being an Organization admin grants no access to any Team's Results

The Organization admin role (WorkOS's org-level `admin`) covers administration only: Teams, Leads, and People. Seeing a Team's Results, comments, or Actions requires a Membership in that Team, whatever the person's Organization role. Admins are often the people members worry about most. If the admin role could read every Team's Results, it would undercut "trust before features" and put leadership roll-ups (Release 3) in through a side door.
# Workspace layout and toolchain: pnpm, TypeScript 7, oxc tools, and Alchemy v2's Effect runtime kept inside the adapters

**Workspace.** pnpm workspaces with a `catalog:` of exact pins, on Node 24 LTS (`.node-version`). Pinned at: `effect` and all `@effect/*` 4.1.2, `alchemy` and `@alchemy.run/*` 2.0.0-beta.85, `typescript` 7.0.2, and exact `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` versions. The Effect and Alchemy pins move only together, in a PR of their own, because both are marked unstable or beta.

**Packages.**

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/domain` | Schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `pulses/`, `rounds/`, `answering/`, `results/`, `actions/`, `privacy/`), schedule and Result calculations | `effect` only |
| `packages/api` | The HttpApi declaration shared by server and client | `domain` |
| `packages/cloudflare` | Adapters (Organization DO, D1, Queue consumer, `EmailSender`, alarm scheduler) and the two Worker entries: the main Worker and the Submission Worker | `domain`, `api`, `emails` (the Queue consumer renders email), Alchemy runtime |
| `apps/web` | One Vite 8 project with two entries: the app (React, TanStack Router, Base UI) and the answer page (no React, no HttpApi client: plain `fetch` plus shared Schemas) | `api`, `domain` (Schemas) |
| `packages/emails` | Email templates | `domain` |
| `infra` | The Alchemy stack and stages (`pr-<n>`, `staging`, `production`) | everything |

**Cloudflare runtime.** Workers, the Durable Object, the Queue consumer, and Cron are defined with Alchemy v2's Effect runtime, but only in `packages/cloudflare`. If the beta fails us, replacing it with a hand-written bridge of about 100 lines touches only that package.

**Tooling.**
- TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler) with `tsc -b` and project references. Settings: `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
- `@effect/tsgo` provides Effect diagnostics.
- oxfmt formats. oxlint lints, with type-aware rules from `oxlint-tsgolint`.
- A local `jsPlugins` package, `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat`, bans `cloudflare:*` and Alchemy imports in `domain` and `api`, and holds the privacy query lint (no `rowid`, no unordered reads of anonymous tables, no joins between anonymous tables and Participation or Invitation).
- The boundary is also enforced by dependencies: `domain` declares only `effect` and uses `types: []`.

**Tests.** Vitest with `@effect/vitest` everywhere:
- domain and API tests in plain Node with in-memory layers and `HttpApiTest`;
- adapter tests through `@alchemy.run/test` `Test.make({ dev: true })` on local workerd;
- smoke tests with `Test.make()` on the PR stage;
- Playwright end-to-end tests on the PR stage.

`vitest-pool-workers` is not used, and there is no hand-edited wrangler config.

**Answer entry (measured in the answer-page prototype, 2026-11-07).** The answer entry is prerendered static HTML with inline CSS and a small plain TypeScript controller, with no React, Preact, or Base UI. Measured with Lighthouse mobile (slow 4G, 4× CPU), the time until the Question text appears was 1.12 s with this approach, 1.35 s with Preact, 1.61 s with React, and 1.90 s with React plus Base UI. The token request starts from an inline script in `<head>`, and Effect Schema (23.5 KB gzip) loads after first paint. Budget: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip on the critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB, 1 request before first paint and 2 before the Question text. A Lighthouse CI gate checks FCP ≤ 800 ms, LCP ≤ 1.3 s, and TBT ≤ 50 ms.

## Considered Options

- **TypeScript 5.9 or 6.** Rejected: 7.0.2 is npm `latest`, Effect recommends it, and Alchemy is built against it. 6.0 is the end of the JavaScript-based compiler line. Our tools (oxc, Vite/rolldown, Vitest) don't depend on the old compiler API.
- **Biome, or ESLint with Prettier.** Rejected in favour of oxlint and oxfmt. oxlint's `jsPlugins` let the boundary and privacy rules be ordinary lint rules, and `oxlint-tsgolint` gives type-aware rules on TypeScript 7.
- **A hand-written Effect bridge from day one.** Deferred: Alchemy's runtime removes the bridge code. Keeping it in one package makes the switch cheap if we need it.

## Consequences

A spike on a preview stage verifies this before the walking skeleton is built. It checks the Organization DO with `SqliteClient`, transactions, migrations, and an alarm, a Queue consumer with a dead-letter queue, the Submission Worker with every log setting off, the deployed cold start, and `tsc -b` with project references on TypeScript 7.0.2.

# Infrastructure: Alchemy stack and preview stages

The stack is `infra/alchemy.run.ts` (stack name `Surveybeat`). Run Alchemy from the repository root, because the Durable Object's SQL migrations are found relative to the working directory.

| Stage | Hostnames |
| --- | --- |
| `pr-<n>` | `pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app`, `pr-<n>.submit.surveybeat.app` |
| `production` | `app.surveybeat.app`, `submit.surveybeat.app` |
| any other (personal dev, tests) | workers.dev |

A new custom hostname takes about a minute to get its certificate, so the first requests fail the TLS handshake. `infra/scripts/smoke.ts` retries.

## Commands

```sh
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build        # the Main Worker serves apps/web/dist
pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-yourname     # `alchemy deploy infra/alchemy.run.ts`
pnpm infra:destroy --stage dev-yourname
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... pnpm check:observability --stage dev-yourname
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... pnpm test:preview-privacy --stage dev-yourname <main-url> <submission-url>
E2E_BASE_URL=<main-url> pnpm test:e2e      # once: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium
```

## Preview stages in CI

`.github/workflows/preview.yml` deploys `pr-<number>` on every push to a pull request, smoke tests the stage, and destroys it when the pull request closes. It needs the repository secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`. Fork pull requests are skipped. After the deploy, two jobs run against the stage:

- `preview-privacy` reads back the Submission Worker's settings (below) on every PR. When the PR touches `packages/cloudflare`, `infra`, the answer entry (`apps/web/answer.html`, `src/answer`, `src/messages`, `vite.config.ts`), the dependency pins or this workflow, it also runs the canary sweep (`infra/tests/privacy/canary-sweep.ts`).
- `e2e` runs the Playwright tests in `infra/tests/e2e/` (the SPEC §7 flow, which grows with the slices).

## Workers Logs are sampled at 1%

The account's Workers Logs are rate limited: `GET /accounts/{id}/observability/usage/limit` (`cf observability usage-limit get`) reports `status: "limited"` and `sample_rate: 0.01`, so Cloudflare keeps a 1% head-based sample of every Worker's events (the documented behaviour once an account passes its daily limit; `resets_at` is null, so do not count on it ending). A single request has a 99% chance of leaving no event. This is why the spike's Main Worker, with logs on and about 25 requests, never showed up.

The canary sweep therefore sends its canary 1000 times to each Worker (all lost with probability 0.99^1000 ≈ 4·10⁻⁵). It polls for up to 10 minutes until the Main Worker's canary is found (the positive control), then asserts that the Submission Worker produced zero events and that its canary is in no event. If logging were on, about 10 of its 1000 requests would be kept, so zero is meaningful. Checked on 2026-11-07 on a workers.dev stage: the sweep passed in 90 seconds (12 Main events found), and with the Submission Worker's logs switched on it failed (7 events, canary found).

## State store (one-time bootstrap)

Alchemy state lives in the `alchemy-state-store` Worker of the Cloudflare account. In CI (`CI=true`) a missing or outdated store fails the run on purpose, so provision or upgrade it from a laptop logged in with `alchemy profile`:

```sh
pnpm exec alchemy state bootstrap -c infra/alchemy.run.ts
```

Done on 2026-11-07: the existing store was v7 and was upgraded to v8.

## Deployed observability settings

Alchemy turns observability on when the prop is omitted, so the Submission Worker sets every channel off. `check-observability.ts` reads the settings back from the Cloudflare API and fails if `observability.enabled`, `logs.enabled`, `traces.enabled` or `logpush` is on, or a tail consumer is attached. `logs.invocation_logs` and `persist` always read `true` while their channel is off, and no API call changes that (tested with the script-settings and Workers PATCH endpoints), so they count only when their channel is on.

## Email

Transactional email goes through one Queue consumer on the Main Worker (`packages/cloudflare/src/EmailDelivery.ts`). Each send's state lives in its Organization's Durable Object (`email_send`), and the transitions are in `packages/domain/src/email` (ADR 0006).

| Stage | What a send does | Provisioned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `production` | Sends through Cloudflare Email Sending from `team@notify.surveybeat.app` | The `notify.surveybeat.app` sending subdomain, the `send_email` binding, the `EmailEvents` queue, and its event subscription |
| `pr-<n>`, personal, `test_*` | Renders the message and records it in the stage's D1 table `captured_email`. Sends nothing. | No sending subdomain, no `send_email` binding, no event subscription |

The sending subdomain makes Cloudflare create its DKIM, SPF, DMARC, MX, and bounce records under `notify.surveybeat.app`. Nothing at the apex changes: its SPF, DMARC, MX, and mail-server records belong to the existing mail setup and are not managed by Alchemy. Message previews in the Cloudflare activity log are off (`previewEnabled: false`), because messages will carry Invitation links.

Read what a PR stage would have sent (the database id is the stack output `databaseId`):

```sh
cf d1 query <databaseId> --sql "SELECT recipient, subject, text FROM captured_email ORDER BY captured_at DESC LIMIT 10"
```

No stage other than `production` can send real mail. To try real sending elsewhere, change `sendsRealEmail` in `packages/cloudflare/src/Email.ts` on a throwaway branch and deploy a personal stage. That stage then also claims `notify.surveybeat.app` and its event subscription, so destroy it before production is deployed.

**Send states.** `pending → sending → sent | failed(reason)`. A delivery takes a two-minute lease before calling the provider, and the call times out after 30 seconds. A clear rejection (`E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and other coded errors) returns the send to `pending` and the message is retried after 30 s, 60 s, and 120 s; the fourth rejection fails it. Permanent rejections (`E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED`, sender and header errors) fail at once. An error without a code, a timeout, or a lease that expired with no outcome fails the send as `unknown`, and it is never resent automatically. A message the queue dead-letters fails its send too (`abandoned`, or `rejected` after earlier rejections).

**Bounces and complaints.** Alchemy's `Cloudflare.Queues.Subscription` with the `email.sending` source subscribes the `EmailEvents` queue to `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `message.rejected`, and `message.failed` for the sending subdomain. The consumer finds the send through the D1 table `email_message` (provider message id → Organization and send) and fails it with the event's reason.

**Fallback.** Postmark would be a second `EmailSender` adapter in `packages/cloudflare`, with its webhooks parsed into the same delivery events (`docs/research/cloudflare-email-sending.md` §9). It is not built.
import * as Cloudflare from "@alchemy.run/cloudflare";
import { Database, MainWorker, ProductionEmail, SubmissionWorker } from "@surveybeat/cloudflare";
import * as Alchemy from "alchemy";
import * as Effect from "effect/Effect";

/**
 * One stack per stage: `pr-<n>` for every pull request, later `staging` and `production`.
 * State lives in the Cloudflare state store, so CI and laptops see the same stages.
 */
export default Alchemy.Stack(
  "Surveybeat",
  {
    providers: Cloudflare.providers(),

name: Preview

# One stage per pull request: `pr-<number>`, on pr-<number>.app.surveybeat.app and
# pr-<number>.submit.surveybeat.app. Destroyed when the pull request closes.
# Alchemy state lives in the Cloudflare state store (see docs/infra.md for the one-time bootstrap).

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]

permissions:
  contents: read

# One run per pull request at a time, and never cancel a running deploy or destroy.
concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  STAGE: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}

jobs:
  deploy:
    # Fork pull requests get no secrets.
    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build the web app
        run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
      - name: Deploy the stage
        run: pnpm exec alchemy deploy infra/alchemy.run.ts --stage "$STAGE" --yes --no-input
      - name: Smoke test
        run: node infra/scripts/smoke.ts "https://$STAGE.app.surveybeat.app" "https://$STAGE.submit.surveybeat.app"

  # Preview-stage privacy checks (privacy suite design, issue #25): A7 on the deployed stage.
  # The read-back runs on every PR. The canary sweep is required only when a PR touches what the
  # Submission path is built from; on any other PR the step passes without running.
  preview-privacy:
    needs: deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Read back the Submission Worker's deployed settings
        run: pnpm check:observability --stage "$STAGE"
      - name: Does this PR touch the Submission path?
        id: paths
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          changed=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
          echo "$changed"
          if echo "$changed" | grep -qE '^(packages/cloudflare/|infra/|apps/web/(answer\.html|vite\.config\.ts|src/answer/|src/messages/)|pnpm-workspace\.yaml|pnpm-lock\.yaml|\.github/workflows/preview\.yml)'; then
            echo "required=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "required=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No Submission path changes: the canary sweep is not required for this PR."
          fi
      - name: Canary sweep with a positive control
        if: steps.paths.outputs.required == 'true'
        run: pnpm test:preview-privacy --stage "$STAGE" "https://$STAGE.app.surveybeat.app" "https://$STAGE.submit.surveybeat.app"

  # The SPEC §7 end-to-end flow on the PR stage. It grows as the slices land.
  e2e:
    needs: deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Install Chromium
        run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: End-to-end tests
        run: pnpm test:e2e
        env:
          E2E_BASE_URL: https://${{ env.STAGE }}.app.surveybeat.app
      - if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: e2e-traces
          path: test-results/e2e
          retention-days: 7

  destroy:
    if: github.event.action == 'closed' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      # The head commit, because the merge ref is gone once the pull request is merged.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
      - name: Destroy the stage
        run: pnpm exec alchemy destroy infra/alchemy.run.ts --stage "$STAGE" --yes --no-input

An Organization admin builds Teams, and a Lead adds members by email.

- An Organization admin can create and rename Teams, assign and remove Leads, and add and remove People. Being an admin grants no access to any Team's Results (ADR 0003).

The deployable walking skeleton: both Workers, the Organization Durable Object, D1, and Queues, deployed to a fresh stage for every PR and destroyed when the PR closes.

- An Alchemy v2 stack in `infra` with:

-- The global index for sign-in (SPEC §6.2, ADR 0002): what must be looked up before the
-- Organization is known. Persons themselves live in their Organization's Durable Object; these
-- rows only route to them. Emails are stored normalised (trimmed, lower case). No survey content.

-- Organization → its WorkOS organization (one to one), and the name the picker shows.
CREATE TABLE organization_index (
  organization_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  workos_organization_id TEXT UNIQUE
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- One row per Person. `workos_user_id` is NULL until the Person first signs in and is linked by
-- an exact match on a verified email; after that the row is found by user, not by email.
CREATE TABLE person_index (
  organization_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  person_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (email = lower(trim(email))),
  workos_user_id TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id, person_id)
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- WorkOS user → Persons.
CREATE INDEX person_index_by_user ON person_index (workos_user_id) WHERE workos_user_id IS NOT NULL;
-- email → Organizations, for Persons not yet linked.
CREATE INDEX person_index_unlinked_by_email ON person_index (email) WHERE workos_user_id IS NULL;
-- A WorkOS user is at most one Person per Organization.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX person_index_one_per_organization
  ON person_index (organization_id, workos_user_id) WHERE workos_user_id IS NOT NULL;

-- "Create an Organization" is idempotent per WorkOS user: the first claim wins, and every retry
-- or double submit finishes that same Organization.
CREATE TABLE organization_claim (
  workos_user_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  organization_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  admin_person_id TEXT NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- The deny list: WorkOS sessions (`sid`) signed out or revoked. Checked on every request, because
-- an access token stays valid until it expires. Keyed by session, not Organization, since one
-- session moves between Organizations when it is refreshed into another one.
CREATE TABLE revoked_session (
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  revoked_at INTEGER NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID;

# The Organization Durable Object owns each Round's state and schedule, and Release 1 uses no Workflows

SPEC §6.2 suggests a Workflow per Round plus an hourly Cron job that creates Rounds. Instead, each Round's state, together with a schedule table of its due jobs (open, send for a time zone, remind, close, compute, notify, create the next Round), lives in the Organization's Durable Object. One DO alarm is always set to the earliest due job, and the alarm handler runs each job as an idempotent DO method in the same transaction as the state change it makes. A daily Cron job only wakes every Organization's DO to repair a missing alarm.

This keeps one owner and one store for each Round. With Workflows, step results would be persisted outside the DO, a Workflow-to-DO bridge would have to be built for Effect, and every transition would span two systems that can each run a step twice. The cost is a small scheduling loop of our own on top of the alarm's at-least-once retries.

## Consequences

- A local time becomes UTC when its job is scheduled, using IANA time zones. Send times are restricted to 06:00–21:00 local.
- Exactly-once sending is enforced on the Invitation row (`pending → sending → sent | failed(reason)`, with a lease). A lease that expires with no outcome becomes `failed: unknown` and is shown to the Lead with Resend, never resent automatically. So a crash can cause a visible gap but never a duplicate.
- Workflows remain an option for later long-running jobs, such as AI theme generation in Release 2, if a DO alarm is a poor fit.

# Each request checks revoked sessions in D1 and the Person's status in the Organization Durable Object

A WorkOS access token is verified locally and stays valid until it expires (about 5 minutes), even after its session is revoked. To make revocation take effect on the next request, the Main Worker adds its own deny check after the JWT check. It has two parts, each kept where its data already lives:

- **Revoked sessions are in D1** (`revoked_session`, keyed by the token's `sid`). Sign-out writes the row before it redirects to WorkOS's logout. The key is the session, not the Organization, because one WorkOS session moves between Organizations when it is refreshed into another one, and an Organization-less session (first sign-in, the picker, "Create an Organization") has no Durable Object to ask. D1 has a single primary and read replication stays off, so the next read sees the write.
- **"Person removed" and "Membership ended" are in the Organization's Durable Object**, which owns People and Memberships (ADR 0006). When the token is scoped to an Organization, the check asks that object for the user's active Person. Mirroring removals and Membership end dates into D1 would add a second copy that can lag the first, and the Durable Object is called on nearly every Organization request anyway.

The D1 read and the Organization lookup run concurrently, then the Durable Object is asked.

## Considered Options

- **KV for the deny list.** Rejected by SPEC §6.2: KV is eventually consistent, so a revoked session could keep working for up to a minute in other locations.
- **Everything in the Organization Durable Object.** Rejected: sessions without an Organization would have no place to be revoked, and a session refreshed into another Organization would escape a revocation recorded in the first.
- **Everything in D1.** Rejected: Person and Membership state would have to be copied from the Durable Object on every change.
- **Calling WorkOS `revokeSession` and relying on short tokens.** Not enough: the token keeps working until it expires.

## Consequences

- Every signed-in request costs one D1 read, plus one Durable Object call when it is in an Organization.
- `revoked_session` rows can be deleted once they are older than the longest WorkOS session. Nothing prunes them yet.
- Slice 04 must deactivate the WorkOS organization membership when it removes a Person, so that AuthKit stops putting the user back into that Organization at sign-in.
EOF
